task_name: Reading gate 1's state, derived and never stored

rubric.result: The objective promises three answers for a checkout, and each one is produced by a line of the diff: no execution spec (`specs.mostRecent` null -> `SpecFreezeState.NO_SPEC`, read-spec-freeze.ts:66-68), a draft with the yardstick's findings (`!spec.isFrozen()` -> DRAFT with `findings: spec.findings()`, which is the plugin's own `analyzeSpecFreeze` reached through `EpicSpec`, line 70-74), and a frozen spec with its date and its pull request (`frozenOn: spec.frozenOn()` plus `branch.current(root)` then `pullRequests.openOfBranch({branch, repository})`, lines 76-80). The port ordering the task's prose fixes is honoured: neither `branch` nor `pullRequests` is reached on the draft or the no-spec path. One sentence of the task's prose body is not delivered and is not deliverable: 'This task also brings EpicSpec#findings() and #isFreezable() under test' — `findings()` is covered through the query, but `isFreezable()` is never called by `ReadSpecFreeze`, and covering it here would need either a domain test of its own (`conventions/testing.md` antipattern: 'A test of the domain reachable from the application layer') or a call with no consumer. It is outside the `**Objective:**` sentence and unreachable from it, so it produces no finding.

The plan's TDD line names `it('a spec with a clarification marker still pending answers draft with the module line and raw text, and asks neither git nor github')` and the test in the diff carries that name verbatim (test file line 255). Its body matches the written assertion clause by clause: the mother `draftWithPendingClarification()` puts `- [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: who signs the freeze?]` on line 9 of the spec text (counted: title, blank, handoff, date, state, blank, `## Hipótesis`, blank, the marker) and gives `## Hipótesis` a bet; the assertion is `state` DRAFT and `findings` `toEqual` exactly one `FreezeFinding({code: CLARIFICATION_MARKER, line: 9, detail: '- [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: who signs the freeze?]'})` — same input, same expected value, one element only; and `branch.asked`/`pullRequests.asked` are both asserted empty. The boundary pair the plan asks for is in the same `it`: `draftWithClarificationResolved()` is the identical text with that one line deleted, and asserts DRAFT with `findings` `toEqual([])`. The line number and the detail come from the real `analyzeSpecFreeze` (groom.js:151, `{ line: i + 1, raw: raw.trim() }`), not from a value the test invented.

The Contract block for `backend/src/application/queries/read-spec-freeze.ts` is matched symbol by symbol: `ReadSpecFreezeParams` with readonly `root: CheckoutRoot` and `repository: RepositoryName` and a single destructured object parameter; `SpecFreezeState` as `Object.freeze({NO_SPEC: 'no-spec', DRAFT: 'draft', FROZEN: 'frozen'} as const)` — the three literal values spelled exactly as the plan writes them; `SpecFreezeRead` with the five readonly fields in the declared order and the declared types (`state`, `spec: EpicSpec | null`, `findings: FreezeFinding[]`, `frozenOn: string | null`, `pullRequest: ReviewedPullRequest | null`); `ReadSpecFreeze` with `constructor({specs, branch, pullRequests})` over the three ports and `async execute(params: ReadSpecFreezeParams): Promise<SpecFreezeRead>`. The port methods called exist with those signatures (`epic-specs.ts` `mostRecent(root)`, `epic-branch.ts` `current(root)`, `pull-requests.ts` `openOfBranch({branch, repository})`). No error or constant beyond these is declared. The one symbol beyond the block, `export type SpecFreezeStateValue`, is the established idiom of this backend for a frozen vocabulary (`freeze-finding.ts:7`, `implementation-state.ts:17`, `delivery-policy.ts:3`) and only names the inline type the block itself writes.

Rows the diff bears on: D-13 (no phase is stored) — every answer is computed inside `execute` and nothing is written anywhere, no adapter and no record is touched. D-11 (a yardstick is imported from the plugin, never reimplemented) — the draft's findings are `spec.findings()`, which delegates to the plugin's `analyzeSpecFreeze`/`HYPOTHESIS_REASONS` through `EpicSpec`; the query grows no second opinion about clarification markers or the hypothesis, and the test fixtures are fed to that real parser rather than to a reimplementation. D-10 (everything new under `backend/` is TypeScript) — both new files are `.ts` with erasable syntax only, and `npm run typecheck` is in the task's verification. D-16 (cmux leaves the backend) — no module here names cmux. D-6, D-7, D-22 and D-23 speak about the gate's act and the pull request being written to; this task only reads (`openOfBranch`), opens nothing and merges nothing. No row is implemented with a value other than the one it states, and no row is reopened.

Exemplars: the query mirrors `backend/src/application/queries/read-implementation-progress.ts` (params object frozen at construction, ports by name in the constructor, a result object declared beside the use case) and the test mirrors `backend/__tests__/application/open-coordinating-session.test.ts` (doubles that `extend` the real port so an uncalled method throws, a `Flow` handed straight to the use case constructor, real value instances rather than doubled values). `conventions/testing.md`: the mothers are named scenarios (`draftWithPendingClarification`, `draftWithHypothesisTemplateCommentOnly`, `frozen`), the assertions are on what the use case returned and on what each port received, values are not doubled, and the fixture is a literal spec document fed to the real reader rather than a reimplemented model of the format. `conventions/architecture.md`: the module sits in `application/queries` (the folder is the discriminator), imports only domain ports and value objects, and depends on no adapter; `conventions/boundaries.md` has no subject here — this diff crosses no edge, assembles no graph and translates nothing outwards. `conventions/style.md`: no comment or docstring, every function hangs off a type, English throughout; the Spanish literals in the fixtures (`**Estado:**`, `**Fecha de congelación:**`, `## Hipótesis`, `CONGELADA`) are the parsed contract `CLAUDE.md` pins and correctly stay. `conventions/simplicity.md`: no guard downstream of a door, no branch for a state that cannot occur. `conventions/decisions.md`: freezability and the freeze date are decided once, in the domain, and read from there. Delivery: no document of either yardstick prescribes a shape of change for a use case with no call site yet (the route is a later task), and nothing is left on an old path. `conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule — (1) closed vocabulary: `SpecFreezeState` is a frozen vocabulary with its value type, no boolean stands in for it, no member is compared by hand, and the only dispatch over a vocabulary (`epic-spec.ts`'s switch, with its raising default) is not in this diff; (2) raw map as the return value of logic: the use case returns the frozen `SpecFreezeRead` class, and the only raw object is `ReviewedPullRequest`, which is the port's own declared shape (`pull-requests.ts:4`) carried through untouched, decided with nowhere — no new defect; (3) two fields that have to agree: absences travel in the type (`spec`, `frozenOn` and `pullRequest` are `| null`, no empty string and no sentinel date) with `state` as the single discriminator — the one tension is the hard-coded `findings: []` on the FROZEN path, reported below as `low`; (4) an error named for where it happens: this diff declares and raises no error, so the rule has no subject. Two clashes declared rather than reported as findings: (a) the plan's `**Tests:**` prescribed two names containing `Hipótesis`, which `backend/__tests__/yardstick.ts` rejects (`character.codePointAt(0)! > 127 && /\p{L}/u.test(character)`), so the plan's control and the repo's automated convention could not both be satisfied — the implementer amended the plan to `Hypothesis`, judged under `alcance`; (b) the plan's prose claims this task brings `EpicSpec#isFreezable()` under test, which `conventions/testing.md`'s ban on domain tests of their own makes impossible from this query.

Does not apply: the diff's only `-` lines are the two in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-14-issue-329-gate-1-the-freeze.md`, which rewrite two prescribed test names in the plan's `**Tests:**` list (`Hipótesis` -> `Hypothesis`). Both new files are additions; no pre-existing test file is touched, so no assertion, case or test that already existed was removed, relaxed or rewritten.

The promised behaviour is produced by `backend/src/application/queries/read-spec-freeze.ts`: the three-way answer, the skipping of `branch`/`pullRequests` on the draft and no-spec paths, and the frozen path's two calls all live there. The scaffolding contributes only inputs and recorders: the mothers are spec text handed to the real `EpicSpec`, whose `findings()` runs the plugin's real `analyzeSpecFreeze` — the asserted `line: 9` and the trimmed detail are computed by production code, not written into a stub — and the doubles only record what they were asked and answer a value the test named. Revert the production file and every one of the five tests fails at the import.

Both declared paths are created and nothing inside them exceeds the task: the production file holds only the four symbols the Contract block names, and the test file holds exactly the five tests `**Tests:**` lists, no more. Nothing named in `### Out of scope` is touched — no `plugin/scripts/`, no skill, no groom, no write to a pull request (`openOfBranch` only reads), no branch created. The plan hunk is an amendment by the implementer and I read it line by line: it changes two test names in this task's `**Tests:**` from `Hipótesis` to `Hypothesis` and nothing else — it removes no route from `**Files:**`, leaves `**TDD:**` and both `**Verification:**` commands untouched, drops no promised test and disarms no control. It is justified: `backend/__tests__/yardstick.ts` fails any test name carrying a non-ASCII letter, so the prescribed names could not exist in this repository, and `CLAUDE.md` puts test names in English while keeping the parsed heading `## Hipótesis` Spanish — which the fixtures do, verbatim, so the real parser still sees the contract heading.

Five new tests, all in `backend/__tests__/application/read-spec-freeze.test.ts`. Deterministic: no clock, no network, no filesystem, no randomness and no sleep — the frozen mother carries the literal date `2026-09-14` in its own text and the assertion pins that same value, so the answer does not depend on today. Isolated: each `it` builds its own `Flow` with fresh doubles, the only shared state is frozen constants (`Mother.ROOT`, `Mother.PULL_REQUEST` via `Object.freeze`), nothing is reset because nothing is mutated across tests, and no order is assumed. Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on what `ReadSpecFreeze.execute` returned or on what a port received — the finding's code, line and detail are computed by the real `analyzeSpecFreeze` reached through `EpicSpec`, not by a stub, and the `asked` assertions pin the production branch that must not reach git or GitHub. The three properties hold, so no `high`. Measured against the text the implementer was given (`control-tower-loop:test-driven-development`, loaded, and its `testing-anti-patterns.md`): no assertion is on a mock's existence or call count for its own sake, no test-only method reaches production, and the doubles are complete against their ports. The one thing that reads against the skill's 'One thing. "and" in name? Split it.' is the first test, which carries two act/assert blocks and an `and` in its name — but the plan's `**TDD:**` line prescribes that exact name and orders the boundary pair inside it, so the implementer could write no other test there; declared here rather than reported.

findings.what: The implementer declares a surviving mutation on the FROZEN branch's `findings: []` (replacing it with `spec.findings()` keeps the suite green) and chose to keep the line and write no test, which is neither of the two repairs `conventions/testing.md` allows. A third route was open and would have killed it without touching the plan's Contract block: derive the field once, the way the DRAFT branch already does, so no untested constant is left in the answer. It does not block — the field has no reader in the FROZEN state (`conventions/simplicity.md`: 'Observability answers to a reader who exists'), so the test that would pin it would pin something nobody consumes, and the Contract block makes the field itself mandatory. Reported at `low` because the declaration is honest and the residue is one constant.
findings.evidence: `state: SpecFreezeState.FROZEN, spec, findings: [], frozenOn: spec.frozenOn(), pullRequest,` — against `conventions/testing.md`'s antipattern 'A surviving mutation left with neither of its two repairs chosen.'
